findings.text: Dentry open binds an allocated file to its path, inode and mapping, samples writeback and superblock errors, acquires access counts and operation vectors, runs permission and lease checks, invokes filesystem open, then derives capability flags and normalizes creation related open flags.

Open progresses through path reference, mode accounting, atomic position marking for regular and directory inodes, operation lookup, security check, notify permission, lease break, default seek plus vector capability assertion, filesystem open call, opened marking, capability refinement from available methods, flag cleanup, readahead init, and direct IO validation.
Path-only opens take a short path that sets path and opened mode, suppresses notification, uses an empty operation table, and returns without access counting or filesystem open.

Pure read opens increment a per inode read count, while write opens on non special files acquire combined inode and mount write access and record writer mode; release reverses exactly the side that was acquired.
Backing files acquire and release an additional write hold on the user visible mount alongside the primary mount, selected through a stored user path.

Mount write acquisition increments the writer count first, waits while a write hold indicator is present, then rechecks readonly state and rolls back with read-only failure if the mount became readonly.

Mount writer accounting runs with preemption disabled around a per cpu counter on symmetric multiprocessor builds or a plain scalar otherwise, with ordered loads around hold polling and readonly evaluation.
Readonly determination first consults a remount-in-progress indicator and otherwise falls back to mount and superblock readonly flags, with ordering against concurrent remount flag updates.

Lease handling is configuration dependent: one variant returns success immediately, the other consults the inode lease context locklessly and only invokes the breaking path when a lease list is non empty, translating read-only and nonblock open mode into lease break attributes.
Operation vector acquisition may fail and yields device absence; notification permission failure, lease failure, filesystem open failure, and late direct IO mismatch all abort the open with cleanup.

Temporary unnamed file creation validates identity mapping, checks directory write and execute permission, requires filesystem temporary creation support, instantiates a child entry under a reserved name, delegates creation, emits open notification once opened, validates openability, and marks the inode linkable unless exclusive.
Backing temporary file helper allocates an empty backing file with caller credentials, pins the user path into it, and delegates to the generic temporary creation path, releasing on failure.

Open permission checks reject missing inodes and symlinks, restrict directory write and execution, restrict device, pipe and socket execution and ignore truncation there, enforce no-execution mounts for regular executable opens, then apply generic permission plus append-only, truncation and no-access-time owner rules.
Device opens are allowed only when neither mount nor superblock disables devices; execution is denied when mount or superblock marks no execution, with a diagnostic for anonymous inodes.

Creation mode is normalized by conditionally dropping set-group-id for non directories under group ownership rules, applying process umask unless access lists or no-umask apply, masking to allowed permission bits, and imposing the requested file type.
Child entry allocation links the new entry under the parent children list while holding the parent lock and taking a locked reference on the parent.
Marking a new temporary inode linkable is done under the inode lock.

Backing asynchronous request carries an embedded kernel control block, a reference count, a pointer to the original control block, an optional end-write callback, embedded work for deferred completion, and a saved result value.

Synchronous backing reads execute the vector read path directly with translated flags, while asynchronous reads clone the control block onto a referenced backing request, submit it, drop the submitter reference, and synchronously clean up unless the operation queued.

Backing completion propagates position, runs the saved end-write step when present, releases one reference, then invokes the original completion; a queued variant defers the same completion to the filesystem direct IO workqueue to serialize metadata updates.
Last reference release drops the held file reference and returns the request object to its dedicated cache.

Vector read entry points require a vector read method and read plus readable capability, accept empty vectors as success without calling the filesystem, verify the range, dispatch to the method, and report access notification on success.

Synchronous vector dispatch builds a control block from file defaults and caller flags, starts at the supplied offset or zero, calls the direction specific vector method, forbids queued return, and writes back the new position.
Backing read validates backing mode, empty input, and direct IO capability, executes under the supplied credentials, and invokes an accessed callback on the original file when configured.
Notification helpers suppress events for self-generated and path-only descriptors, add an execute qualifier for execution opens, and map access and open to their respective event kinds.

Open failure after operation lookup releases the operation reference and the acquired read or write access, drops the path reference, clears cached path and inode pointers, and normalizes unexpected positive status to invalid argument.
Direct IO completion workqueue creation races safely: concurrent creators attempt an atomic install and the loser destroys its own queue.
File reference increment warns if applied to an already released reference, indicating use after final put.
Backing control flag translation preserves only nowait, high priority, data synchronous, synchronous, and append attributes.
Notification suppression holds when the notify-related mode bits equal the non-notify value.
Special file classification covers character, block, first-in first-out, and socket types.
Anonymous file test checks an anonymous inode bit in inode flags.
